newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq shows 3 Iraqis who say they spied for Mossad.
newsitem.headline: Iraq shows 3 Iraqis who say they spied for Mossad.

text.p: Three Iraqis who said they had spied for the Israeli intelligence service Mossad were shown on Iraqi television on Wednesday.
Jammal Majeed Nadr, 41, born in the Kurdish province of Arbil in northern Iraq, appeared on state-run television on Wednesday evening and explained how he was recruited to spy for the Mossad.
Speaking in a relaxed manner, he said he travelled to Turkey five times where he met two Israeli intelligence officers.

Nadr said he collected information about the Iraqi army in exchange for U.S. dollar payments. He said he got the information from his two brothers -- one a retired army colonel and the other doing his military service at the Iraqi Defense Ministry.

Nadr said he was recruited by the Israeli intelligence service through a Kurd living in Arbil, which is in the northern Kurdish region out of direct control of the Iraqi government since the 1991 Gulf War.
The Kurd told Nadr the information was going to the United Nations office in Arbil, but later during a trip to Turkey Nadr was told he had been recruited by the Mossad.
He had also been supplying information about the Iraqi economy, he said on television.
